answer: Eight years of merged commits cannot be faked in an afternoon. Open-source commit history reads that record: commits merged into public repos over eight years. Every commit carries a reviewer, a timestamp, and a project that remembers it, so the jade of the forgery is the public log - append-only, mirrored, checked by strangers. One fake needs eight years of plausible work; a hundred need eight hundred, and the hollow at the heart of each is the reviewer who must be fooled, bribed, or invented. The gale that finishes the job is the merge itself: no merge, no history, no account.
